subject: science
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 2½ hours · Maximum marks: 85 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–17 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 18–27 have two parts of 1 mark each; question 28 is a passage with five 1-mark questions.
Section B: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, 5-mark answers in 80–120 words.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns, true/false or a short passage).

questions.q: Read the passage on Newton's law of gravitation (F = G m1m2/r², where G is the universal gravitational constant) and answer: (1) How does the force change if the distance between two bodies is doubled? (2) Write the value of G in SI units.
questions.answer: (1) It becomes one-fourth (F ∝ 1/r²). (2) G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻².

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: The energy possessed by a body because of its position is called ________ energy, and the energy possessed because of its motion is called ________ energy.
Match: (1) Concave mirror (2) Convex mirror — (a) rear-view mirror (b) periscope (c) headlight reflector (d) magnifying glass
questions.answer: (1) Concave mirror – (c) headlight reflector; (2) Convex mirror – (a) rear-view mirror

Fill in the blanks: The production of an electric current by a changing magnetic field is called ________, and it was discovered by ________.
Write True (T) or False (F): (1) The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood. (2) Red blood cells have a nucleus.
questions.answer: (1) True (2) False — mature RBCs have no nucleus.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: The central nervous system consists of the ________ and the ________.

Read the passage and answer: 'Banana plants grown by farmers are genetically similar to the parent plant. Such plants are produced without the fusion of gametes.' (a) Name the method used to grow genetically similar banana plants. (b) Name two types of asexual reproduction.
questions.answer: (a) Vegetative propagation. (b) Any two: binary fission, budding, spore formation, vegetative propagation.

Write True (T) or False (F): (1) Al₂O₃ and CO₂ both show acidic as well as basic properties. (2) Metals are electropositive and non-metals are electronegative.
questions.answer: (1) False — Al₂O₃ is amphoteric but CO₂ is acidic only. (2) True

sections.title: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: The reddish-brown substance is —
The nail in tube B did not rust because —
Anhydrous calcium chloride in tube C —
Galvanisation means coating iron with —
The experiment shows that rusting needs —

sections.passage: Neha placed three clean iron nails in test tubes. Tube A had some tap water so that the nail was partly in water and partly in air. Tube B had boiled water covered by a layer of oil. Tube C was dry and contained anhydrous calcium chloride. After a week, only the nail in tube A was covered with a flaky reddish-brown substance. Her teacher said that the iron gate at home is painted, and buckets are made of galvanised iron, for the same reason.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write two differences between an electron and a proton.
questions.answer: (1) An electron carries a negative charge (−1), while a proton carries a positive charge (+1). (2) An electron has very small mass (about 1/1840 of a proton) and moves around the nucleus, while a proton is heavy and is found in the nucleus.

questions.q: What are indicators? Name one natural indicator and the source from which it is obtained.
questions.answer: Indicators are substances that show one colour in an acidic solution and a different colour in a basic solution, e.g. litmus, phenolphthalein, methyl orange. Litmus is a natural indicator obtained from lichens (turmeric is another).

questions.q: In a lens of focal length 10 cm the sizes of the image and the object are the same. Name the type of lens and give the distance of the object from the lens.
questions.answer: It is a convex lens, since only a convex lens gives an image of the same size (real and inverted). The object is at 2F, i.e. 2 × 10 = 20 cm from the lens.

or.q: Define (i) visual angle and (ii) power of accommodation.
or.answer: (i) Visual angle is the angle an object makes at the eye; the larger it is, the bigger the object looks. (ii) Power of accommodation is the ability of the eye lens to change its focal length so as to see objects from infinity down to 25 cm clearly.

questions.q: Define the terms (i) osmoregulation and (ii) dialysis.
questions.answer: (i) Osmoregulation is the maintenance of the correct amount of water and mineral ions in the blood and body. (ii) Dialysis is the removal of waste from the blood of a person whose kidneys have failed, using an artificial kidney in which blood flows past a membrane bathed in dialysis fluid.

questions.q: Why is genetic counselling advisable before marriage between close relatives?
questions.answer: Close relatives may carry the same defective recessive gene; their children are more likely to get two copies and suffer from a genetic disorder. Counselling tells the couple the chances so they can decide wisely.

questions.q: Name two adaptations of the lotus to live in water.
questions.answer: Long, spongy stem with air spaces that keeps it afloat and bends with currents; broad floating leaves with a waxy upper surface and stomata on the upper side.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Draw a diagram of a synapse and label the synaptic vesicle, synaptic cleft, synaptic bulb and mitochondrion.
questions.answer: Diagram: the swollen end (synaptic bulb) of one neuron's axon lies close to the dendrite of the next neuron, separated by a narrow gap, the synaptic cleft. Inside the bulb are small round synaptic vesicles containing neurotransmitter and a few mitochondria. When an impulse arrives the vesicles release neurotransmitter into the cleft, which starts an impulse in the next neuron.

questions.q: Describe budding in Hydra with a diagram.
questions.answer: In Hydra a small outgrowth (bud) forms on the side of the body due to repeated cell division. It grows, develops a mouth and tentacles, and finally detaches from the parent to live as a new Hydra. Diagram: parent Hydra with a bud at different stages of growth, then a separated young Hydra.

or.q: Name three plants that grow from the stem, and the kind of stem.
or.answer: Potato (tuber), ginger (rhizome), onion (bulb); also lawn grass (runner).

questions.q: What are genes and what is their chemical nature? What genes will a child with blood group O have?
questions.answer: Genes are the units of heredity, located at fixed points on chromosomes; chemically they are segments of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid). A child with blood group O has the genes ii (one recessive i from each parent).

questions.q: Write four chemical properties of metals with equations.
questions.answer: (1) With oxygen they form basic oxides: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. (2) With water they form hydroxides or oxides and hydrogen: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. (3) With dilute acids they give hydrogen: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. (4) A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its salt: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.

questions.q: What is a functional group? Identify the functional groups in CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃, CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CHO and CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH.
questions.answer: A functional group is an atom or group of atoms that decides the characteristic properties of an organic compound, e.g. –OH, –COOH. The groups are: C=C double bond (alkene); >C=O keto (ketone); –CHO (aldehyde); –COOH (carboxylic acid).

questions.q: What is symbiosis? Give an example. How is commensalism different from symbiosis (mutualism)?
questions.answer: Symbiosis is the close living together of two organisms of different species, e.g. alga and fungus in lichen, or bees and flowers. In mutualism both partners benefit; in commensalism one benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed (sucker fish on a shark).

questions.q: What is biomagnification? How did DDT reduce the population of pelican birds?
questions.answer: Biomagnification is the increase in concentration of a non-biodegradable chemical at each higher trophic level. DDT sprayed on crops reached the water (0.2 ppm) and passed through algae and fish into pelicans (1700 ppm). The high DDT in the birds made their egg shells thin, so the eggs broke before hatching and the population fell.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is a unit? List the characteristics of a good unit. Why were units based on parts of the body given up, and how did standard units develop?
questions.answer: A unit is a standard quantity (scale) in terms of which a physical quantity is measured; value = number × unit. A good unit is relevant, convenient and well defined. Units such as the hand span, foot or cubit differ from person to person, so they were arbitrary and gave results that could not be reproduced, causing disputes in trade. Rulers fixed standards (Egyptian standard cubit, Henry I's yard), but these changed with rulers. After the French Revolution the decimal metric system was made, with standard metre and kilogram kept near Paris (Metre Convention, 1875). CGS and MKS systems followed, and in 1960 the International System of Units (SI) was adopted with seven base units, now defined by constants of nature (e.g. the metre through the speed of light).

questions.q: Name the compounds used to preserve biological specimens and to ripen fruit, and give their structures. Name the acids in vitamin C and in citrus fruits. Explain homologous series with an example.
questions.answer: Formalin, a solution of methanal (formaldehyde) H–CHO, preserves specimens. Fruit is ripened with ethene, H₂C=CH₂ (the NIOS text also names ethyne, acetylene HC≡CH, for this). Vitamin C contains ascorbic acid; citrus fruits contain citric acid. A homologous series is a group of compounds with the same functional group and general formula in which successive members differ by –CH₂–, with similar chemical properties and gradually changing physical properties — methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈ (alkanes, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂).
